<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Constructing strong oxide‐support interaction (SOSI) is compelling for modulating the atomic configurations and electronic structures of supported catalysts. Herein, ultrafine iridium oxide nanoclusters (≈1 nm) are anchored on vanadium oxide support (IrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /V
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    ) via SOSI. The as made catalyst, with a unique distorted IrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    structure, is discovered to significantly boost the performance for pH‐universal oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Based on experimental results and theoretical calculations, the distorted IrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    active sites with flexible redox states in IrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /V
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    server as electrophilic centers balance the adsorption of oxo‐intermediates and effectively facilitate the process of OO coupling, eventually propelling the fast turnover of water oxidation. As a result, IrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /V
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    demonstrates not only ultralow overpotentials at 10 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    (266 mV, pH = 0; 329 mV, pH = 7; 283 mV, pH = 14) for OER, but also high‐performance overall water electrolysis over a broad pH range, with a potential of mere 1.50 V (pH = 0), 1.65 V (pH = 7) or 1.49 V (pH = 14) at 10 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    . In addition, SOSI can simultaneously secure the distorted active sites and thus remarkably improving the catalytic stability, making it a promising strategy to develop high‐performance catalytic systems.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Strong Oxide‐Support Interaction over IrO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    /V
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    O
                    <sub>5</sub>
                    for Efficient pH‐Universal Water Splitting
